mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 4.5% for three consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, which raises discount rates and reduces present value of future corporate earnings, leading to negative S&P 500 forward returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative (p > 0.10) in periods where FEDFUNDS > 4.5% for three months.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) exceeding 2% coincides with reduced consumer demand, which negatively impacts corporate revenues and earnings, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative when GDPC1 falls by more than 2% year-over-year.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained rise in the unemployment rate above 6% for two consecutive months signals weakening labor market conditions, which reduces consumer spending and corporate profit margins, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when UNRATE exceeds 6% for two months.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the industrial production index (INDPRO) of more than 1% for three consecutive months indicates contraction in manufacturing output, which reduces corporate earnings and increases recession risk, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: INDPRO monthly change < -1% for 3 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative during three consecutive months of INDPRO declines greater than 1%.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in FEDFUNDS and a decline in CPIAUCSL (core inflation) below 1.5% signals a disinflationary tightening, which increases real interest rates and depresses equity valuations, resulting in negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are not significantly negative when FEDFUNDS is rising and CPIAUCSL < 1.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A strong positive correlation between real personal income (proxied by PAYEMS growth) and S&P 500 returns over the past 12 months suggests a wealth effect mechanism; if PAYEMS growth turns negative while housing starts (HOUST) are rising, it indicates shifting demand composition, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 5 trading days as investors anticipate a housing-driven rebound.
candidate_trigger: PAYEMS growth turns negative AND HOUST growth turns positive
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are not significantly positive when PAYEMS growth turns negative and HOUST growth turns positive.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the unemployment rate above 5% combined with a decline in industrial production (INDPRO) below -0.5% for two consecutive months signals a synchronized labor and supply shock, which increases recession probability and leads to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
candidate_trigger: UNRATE > 5% AND INDPRO monthly change < -0.5% for 2 consecutive months
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly negative during two consecutive months of UNRATE > 5% and INDPRO < -0.5%.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) above trend by more than 1% for four consecutive quarters signals a robust demand environment, which supports corporate earnings and justifies higher equity valuations, resulting in positive S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days regardless of regime.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are not significantly positive when GDPC1 is above trend by more than 1% for four consecutive quarters.
